questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'What Is a Constitution' refers to.
questions.a: A constitution is the supreme rulebook of a state: it sets the structure of government, divides its powers, lists the rights of citizens and the duties of rulers, and stands above every ordinary law.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'What Is a Constitution'.
questions.a: A constitution is the game's rulebook for the nation: players and referees alike must play by it.

questions.q: Under which section is 'What Is a Constitution' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Making of the Indian Constitution' refers to.
questions.a: India's Constitution was framed by the Constituent Assembly of elected and nominated members between 1946 and 1949; committees debated every clause, and it came into force on 26 January 1950.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Making of the Indian Constitution'.
questions.a: The Constitution was not decreed but deliberated: years of debate gave it the weight of a people's own choice.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Making of the Indian Constitution' taught, and from which source text?

Explain in your own words what 'The Preamble and Its Values' refers to.
questions.a: The Preamble opens the Constitution by declaring India a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic that secures justice, liberty, equality and fraternity for all its citizens.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Preamble and Its Values'.
questions.a: The Preamble is the Constitution in one breath: a summary of the nation's goals and promises.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'The Preamble and Its Values', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: preamble = sovereign + socialist + secular + democratic + republic

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Constitution in Daily Life' refers to.
questions.a: The Constitution touches daily life: it guarantees the rights you exercise at school and street, protects minorities, allows amendment by special procedure, and reminds every official that power is borrowed, not owned.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Constitution in Daily Life'.
questions.a: The Constitution works when citizens use it: rights claimed and duties done keep it alive.
